cohort: The study included 50 pregnant patients diagnosed with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) and 50 pregnant patients with pre-existing diabetes.
finding: Patients with GDM had significantly lower FT3 and FT4 levels, and higher TSH, TGab, and TPOab levels compared to pregnant patients with pre-existing diabetes, which was associated with higher incidence of adverse pregnancy outcomes (premature delivery, post-term birth, cesarean section) and lower intellectual levels in their infants at six-month follow-up.
mod_finding: The total incidence rate of cesarean section was significantly higher in patients with GDM compared to diabetic pregnant patients.
